slides.texte_overlay:
7 subtle behaviors that make
people take you seriously
Arriving prepared. Notes ready, question in mind, the document already read. Preparation shows before you speak, and people instantly treat you as someone who matters.
Saying "I don't know, I'll find out." Pretending to know everything destroys trust. Admitting a gap and coming back with the answer builds credibility fast.
Writing clear, short messages. No walls of text, no five exclamation marks. A tidy three-line email makes you look like someone who thinks clearly and values people's time.
Speaking from real knowledge. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having real facts instead of loud opinions makes people listen when I speak.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Having real facts instead of opinions makes people listen when I speak.

slides.texte_overlay: Not laughing at your own jokes before the end. Deliver it straight, let them laugh. Confidence in your own words, even small ones, signals that you're worth listening to.
Keeping your appointments with yourself. The gym session, the study hour, the early night. People who respect their own commitments are taken seriously by others too.
Disagreeing calmly and with a reason. "I see it differently, here's why." No sarcasm, no eye rolling. Calm disagreement is one of the clearest signs of a serious person.
